findings.evidence: The statement at line 906 is existential for each `n`; `WeightString.lean:308` defines `lieModuleEquivOfHasPrimitiveVectorWith` with primitive-vector hypotheses on both modules, so these results do not by themselves classify every finite-dimensional irreducible.
findings.fix: Narrow the conclusion to existence and uniqueness among irreducible modules carrying a primitive vector of the specified highest weight, or cite and state the missing exhaustiveness theorem if one exists.
findings.issue: The `exists_isIrreducible_hasPrimitiveVectorWith` docstring claims this “settles the classification of the finite-dimensional irreducibles of sl₂: exactly one for each n,” but the theorem proves only existence, while the cited WeightString results prove uniqueness only for modules already carrying a primitive vector of weight `n`; no cited result establishes that every finite-dimensional irreducible has such a vector.

summary: One theorem docstring overstates the scope of the results by claiming an exhaustive classification of finite-dimensional irreducibles.
